title: Characterizing Crowds to Better Optimize Worker Recommendation in Crowdsourced Testing

edges.target: ExReDiv (Cui et al.)
edges.ref: [5] Q. Cui, J. Wang, G. Yang, M. Xie, Q. Wang, M. Li, "Who should be selected to perform a task in crowdsourced testing?" COMPSAC'17, pp. 75-84.
edges.evidence: ExReDiv [5]: This is a weight-based crowd worker recommendation approach. It linearly combines experience strategy ... relevance strategy ... and diversity strategy

edges.target: MOOSE (Cui et al.)
edges.ref: [6] Q. Cui, S. Wang, J. Wang, Y. Hu, Q. Wang, M. Li, "Multiobjective crowd worker selection in crowdsourced testing," SEKE'17, pp. 218-223.
edges.evidence: MOOSE [6]: This is a multi-objective crowd worker recommendation, which can maximize the coverage of test requirement, maximize the test experience of the selected crowd workers, and minimize the cost.

edges.target: Cocoon (Xie et al.)
edges.ref: [7] M. Xie, Q. Wang, G. Yang, M. Li, "Cocoon: Crowdsourced testing quality maximization under context coverage constraint," ISSRE'17, pp. 316-327.
edges.evidence: Cocoon [7]: This crowd worker recommendation approach is based on maximizing the testing quality under the test context coverage constraint.

edges.target: STRING test case prioritization (Ledru et al.)
edges.ref: [41] Y. Ledru, A. Petrenko, S. Boroday, N. Mandran, "Prioritizing test cases with string distances," Automated Software Engineering, 19(1), pp. 65-95, 2012.
edges.evidence: Since the original implementation of STRING baseline and TOPIC baseline are not released, we have reimplemented our own version.

edges.target: TOPIC test case prioritization (Thomas et al.)
edges.ref: [42] S. W. Thomas, H. Hemmati, A. E. Hassan, D. Blostein, "Static test case prioritization using topic models," Empirical Software Engineering, 19(1), pp. 182-212, 2014.
edges.evidence: the two baseline methods which are originally designed for test case selection (i.e., STRING and TOPIC) perform bad for crowd worker recommendation.

edges.target: NSGA-II (Deb et al.)
edges.ref: [55] K. Deb, S. Agrawal, A. Pratap, T. Meyarivan, "A fast elitist non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm for multi-objective optimization: Nsga-II," PPSN, Springer, 2000, pp. 849-858.
edges.evidence: MOCOM uses NSGA-II algorithm (i.e., Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II) to optimize the aforementioned four objectives.

edges.target: Bug Detection Rate at k (BDR@k) metric (Cui/Xie et al.)
edges.ref: [5]-[7] Cui et al. COMPSAC'17; Cui et al. SEKE'17; Xie et al. ISSRE'17.
edges.evidence: Following previous studies [5]-[7], we use the commonly-used bug detection rate for the evaluation.

edges.target: Longitudinal (chronological fold) data setup (Bhattacharya & Neamtiu; Tamrawi et al.)
edges.ref: [14] P. Bhattacharya, I. Neamtiu, "Fine-grained incremental learning and multi-feature tossing graphs to improve bug triaging," ICSM'10; [16] Tamrawi et al. FSE'11.
edges.evidence: To simulate the usage of MOCOM in practice, we employ a commonly-used longitudinal data setup [14], [16].

edges.target: HV, IGD, GS quality indicators (Wang, Ali, Yue et al.)
edges.ref: [24] S. Wang, S. Ali, T. Yue, Y. Li, M. Liaaen, "A practical guide to select quality indicators for assessing pareto-based search algorithms in SBSE," ICSE'16, pp. 631-642.
edges.evidence: Three commonly-used quality indicators, i.e., HyperVolume (HV), Inverted Generational Distance (IGD), and Generalized Spread (GS) [24], are applied.

edges.target: Binary solution encoding and standard genetic operators (Wang, Ali, Yue et al.)
edges.ref: [24] S. Wang, S. Ali, T. Yue, Y. Li, M. Liaaen, ICSE'16, pp. 631-642.
edges.evidence: For the evolution of binary encoding for the solutions, we exploit standard operators as described in [24]. We use single point crossover, bitflip mutation

edges.target: GA parameter settings: population 200, 20,000 evaluations (Holland)
edges.ref: [56] J. H. Holland, Genetic algorithms. Scientific American, 1992.
edges.evidence: We configured NSGA-II with the setting of initial population = 200, maximum fitness evaluation (i.e., number of runs) = 20,000 as recommended by [56].

edges.target: Mann-Whitney U test (Witten & Frank)
edges.ref: [52] I. H. Witten, E. Frank, Data Mining: Practical machine learning tools and techniques. Morgan Kaufmann, 2005.
edges.evidence: we use the Mann-Whitney U statistical test [52] to determine if the difference between the BDR@k is statistically significant.

edges.target: Precision/Recall/F-measure and Information Gain feature ranking (Witten & Frank)
edges.ref: [52] I. H. Witten, E. Frank, Data Mining: Practical machine learning tools and techniques. Morgan Kaufmann, 2005.
edges.evidence: We use the three most commonly-used metrics (i.e., Precision, Recall, and F-Measure) [52] ... We first obtain the Information Gain [52] for each feature

edges.target: Recent-activity-predicts-future-behavior finding (Zhou & Mockus)
edges.ref: [38] M. Zhou, A. Mockus, "What make long term contributors: Willingness and opportunity in oss community," ICSE'12; [39] Zhou & Mockus, TSE 41(1), 2015.
edges.evidence: previous work demonstrated the open source developer's recent activity has greater indicative effect on his future behavior than the activity happened long before [38], [39]. Therefore, we further take the timerelated factors

edges.target: Learned bug-revealing probability as selection criterion (Chen et al. ICSE'17)
edges.ref: [44] J. Chen, Y. Bai, D. Hao, Y. Xiong, H. Zhang, B. Xie, "Learning to prioritize test programs for compiler testing," ICSE'17, pp. 700-711.
edges.evidence: First, we should recommend the crowd workers with maximized bug detection probability [44], since they can potentially improve the bug detection performance.

edges.target: Paid-by-participation cost model (softwaretestinghelp crowdsourced-testing page)
edges.ref: [3] http://www.softwaretestinghelp.com/crowdsourced-testing-companies/.
edges.evidence: We suppose all the workers who participate in a test task are equally paid, which is a common practice in real-world crowdsourced testing platforms [3].

edges.target: Cold-start problem / recall limits in recommender systems (Ricci et al.)
edges.ref: [58] F. Ricci, L. Rokach, B. Shapira, P. B. Kantor, Recommender systems handbook. Springer, 2015.
edges.evidence: This is the cold-start problem in recommendation [58], which has not been well solved.

edges.target: Brooks: testing consumes half of project resources
edges.ref: [1] F. Brooks, Jr., The Mythical Man-Month: Essays on Software Engineering. Addison-Wesley, 1995.
edges.evidence: According to Brooks [1], testing a software system consumes half of the resources of any software projects.

edges.target: Harman et al. SBSE survey: >65% of techniques use GA or NSGA-II
edges.ref: [54] M. Harman, S. A. Mansouri, Y. Zhang, "Search-based software engineering: Trends, techniques and applications," ACM Computing Surveys 45(1), p. 11, 2012.
edges.evidence: According to [54], more than 65% optimization techniques in software analysis are based on Genetic Algorithm (for problems with single objective), or NSGA-II

edges.target: Epitropakis et al. Pareto-efficient regression TCP quality-indicator results
edges.ref: [57] M. G. Epitropakis, S. Yoo, M. Harman, E. K. Burke, "Empirical evaluation of pareto efficient multi-objective regression test case prioritisation," ISSTA 2015, pp. 234-245.
edges.evidence: Existing researches on test case selection and worker selection achieve similar results [6], [57]. This further suggests that the results of MOCOM have high quality.

edges.target: Cosine similarity effectiveness on high-dimensional text (Wang et al. ESEM'16)
edges.ref: [34] J. Wang, Q. Cui, Q. Wang, S. Wang, "Towards effectively test report classification to assist crowdsourced testing," ESEM'16, p. 6.
edges.evidence: The reason why we use cosine similarity is that past researches have demonstrated its effectiveness in high-dimensional textual data [13], [34], [53], which is exactly our case.

edges.target: Logistic regression effectiveness in SE classification (DARS, Wang et al.)
edges.ref: [36] J. Wang, Q. Cui, S. Wang, Q. Wang, "Domain adaptation for test report classification in crowdsourced testing," ICSE-SEIP'17, pp. 83-92.
edges.evidence: We employ Logistic Regression as our machine learning model, which is widely reported as effective in many different classfication tasks in software engineering [36], [52].

edges.target: Diversity importance in test selection (Ledru et al. ASE'09 and related)
edges.ref: [40] Y. Ledru, A. Petrenko, S. Boroday, "Using string distances for test case prioritisation," ASE'09, pp. 510-514.
edges.evidence: Third, we should select a set of crowd workers with diverse characteristics [40]-[43], because different workers might explore different areas of the application

edges.target: Elbaum et al.: goal is most bugs for least resources, not all bugs
edges.ref: [59] S. Elbaum, G. Rothermel, J. Penix, "Techniques for improving regression testing in continuous integration development environments," FSE 2014, pp. 235-245.
edges.evidence: the goal is often not "find all bugs" but "find as many bugs using least resources as possible" (which, in our case, is the number of crowd workers) [59].

not_reuse_examples: [4] Hosseini et al. 'four pillars of crowdsourcing' - background definition of crowdsourcing (open call, incentives); nothing adopted or run.
[8]-[23] bug triage / mentor / crowdsourced-development recommendation papers (Anvik, Jeong, Xuan, Mao, Yang ...) - related-work survey only, none used as baseline.
[45]-[51] white-box test case prioritization (QTEP, Rothermel, Yoo & Harman survey, Li/Harman/Hierons ...) - cited only to explain why coverage-based approaches cannot apply.
[25] Henard et al. and [27]-[33] crowdsourced-testing applications (Feng et al. report prioritization, Musson Lync, Gomez ...) - context and motivation citations only.
notes: Empirical SBSE/recommendation paper (TSE-style, 'Review x-y' reviewer markers in text); dataset is authors' own Baidu CrowdTest collection (562 tasks) with no prior-origin ref, so no dataset edge; three of five baselines are the authors' own prior systems, all outperformed; STRING/TOPIC were reimplemented by the authors.
